collection_summary: This instance is a source-defined ground truth listing the 15 films that have won at least 8 competitive Academy Awards per Wikipedia's 'List of Academy Award–winning films' master article. For each film the staged row records the Year of Release, the Total Oscars Won (the aggregation cell — pre-aggregated COUNT of competitive Academy Award wins per film from the master article's Awards column), whether the film also won Best Picture (closed Yes/No vocabulary), and the director(s) per the per-film Wikipedia article. The 15-row universe is fully source-defined via the master article's table filtered to Awards ≥ 8. The schema is designed for aggregation benchmark evaluation: Film is the PK lookup target; Total Oscars Won is the aggregation cell (COUNT-grouped-by-Film, pre-aggregated by source); Best Picture Winner is exact-match from closed 2-value vocab; Director is exact-match text with semicolon-delimited multi-director cells. Cabaret (1972) is the single calibration case: won 8 Oscars but lost Best Picture to The Godfather, making it the only Best Picture=No row in the universe.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_Academy_Award–winning_films): master article supplying universe + filter + 3 of 5 cells per row. The master article's Film / Year / Awards / Nominations table contains all Academy-Award-winning films with their competitive Award counts; the staged universe is the table membership filtered to Awards ≥ 8. The 'Total Oscars Won' cell is taken verbatim from the master Awards column (a pre-aggregated COUNT(*) over competitive Oscar wins per film); the 'Best Picture Winner' status is determined via the master article's Best-Picture-styling cues (master article highlights / formats Best Picture winners distinctly within its table) and cross-verified against the per-film Wikipedia article's infobox 'Academy Awards' / 'Best Picture' references.
- source_urls[1-15] (15 per-film Wikipedia articles): per-film source supplying Year of Release + Director cells via the per-film infobox. Each per-film article also serves as a verification cross-reference for Total Oscars Won and Best Picture Winner cells.

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 16 = 1 master + 15 per-film articles). Cell-level audit: Film + Total Oscars Won + Best Picture Winner cells can be spot-checked against the master article's table row for that film; Year of Release + Director cells can be spot-checked against the per-film article infobox.

Aggregation category-fit (CRITICAL design point): the Total Oscars Won cell is COUNT(*) over the film's competitive Academy Award wins, pre-aggregated by the master article. This is a SOURCE-PROVIDED aggregate count, NOT a model-side computation from raw per-award rows. The aggregation primitive is honest because the cell is a COUNT-GROUP-BY-Film result, even though the source supplies the pre-computed value rather than requiring the model to compute it from underlying per-award rows. Mirror precedent: us_presidents_count_by_birth_state uses the same pattern — per-state count is pre-aggregated in the master, not computed by the model from raw president records.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass (after pre-staging audit design review — see post-staging cycle-0 notes below). Universe (15 films winning ≥ 8 competitive Academy Awards) is fully source-defined via the master 'List of Academy Award–winning films' Wikipedia article's table filtered to Awards ≥ 8. Per-row attribute cells are verbatim from the master (Film + Total Oscars Won + Best Picture Winner) or grounded by per-film articles (Year of Release + Director). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical iconic films (Ben-Hur 11 Oscars Best Picture, Titanic 11 Oscars Best Picture, LOTR Return 11 Oscars Best Picture, Gone with the Wind 8 Oscars Best Picture, Slumdog Millionaire 8 Oscars Best Picture); mid-difficulty cells include the older Best Picture winners (Gigi 1958, From Here to Eternity 1953, On the Waterfront 1954, My Fair Lady 1964); harder calibration cells include the Cabaret 8-Oscars-but-not-Best-Picture edge case and the less-popularly-known older Best Picture winners (Gigi 1958, From Here to Eternity 1953). Row count (15) clears the 10-row gate comfortably.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected to chip aggregation from gap 3 with a film-domain angle complementing the existing programming_languages_by_decade + us_presidents_count_by_birth_state aggregation precedents.
- Category: aggregation (gap 3 before this staging — `aggregation` at 2 of 5 with programming_languages_by_decade_of_first_appearance + us_presidents_count_by_birth_state; this instance brings aggregation to 3/5 — gap 3 → 2).
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 16 (1 master + 15 per-film articles).
- Expected shape: 15 rows × 5 columns; single PK = Film.
- Domain: Culture/Film — extends the Culture/Film subdomain from 1 staged instance (top_grossing_films_worldwide_per_decade_1980s_2010s) to 2 staged instances (+ 1 registered trial_join_4 = 3 total Film instances).
- Entity class: artifacts/films — existing fine-class (2 staged instances before this; this is the 3rd films-keyed staged instance).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Threshold ≥8 is curator-chosen per audit recommendation; ≥7 would yield 28 rows with more boundary churn; ≥9 would yield only 7 rows below the 10-row gate. (b) Total Oscars Won is COMPETITIVE Academy Award wins only — honorary Oscars, special achievement awards, and Best Foreign Language Film submissions are NOT counted per Wikipedia master article convention. (c) Cabaret (1972) is the only non-Best-Picture-winner in the ≥8 universe (won 8 Oscars but lost Best Picture to The Godfather) — documented as a benchmark calibration case where LLMs may default to 'Yes' for any 8-Oscar film. (d) Director normalization uses semicolon-delimited multi-director format for West Side Story ('Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins') per the per-film article's co-director credit; single-director films use the bare director name. (e) Best Picture Winner uses closed 2-value Yes/No vocabulary. (f) Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022) is NOT in the universe — it won 7 competitive Oscars, below the ≥8 threshold (this was a cycle-0-corrected initial-design error that proposed 8 Oscars for EEAAO; audit identified the correct count is 7). (g) Diacritic preserved in Miloš Forman director cell per per-film article canonical form. (h) operation_type = 'aggregation' per query_category-matching convention (aggregation-category-with-aggregation-operation pattern; aggregation here is COUNT-GROUP-BY-Film).
- Decision: Stage.

Pre-staging audit design review (2026-05-16): audit agent verdict 'Revise Before Cycle-0 Staging' with 5 required fixes all applied: (1) Threshold ≥8 instead of ≥7 — the audit confirmed ≥7 yields 28 rows (more boundary churn including Oppenheimer 2023 7-Oscar Best-Picture-winner and Gravity 2013 7-Oscars-non-Best-Picture); ≥8 yields cleaner 15-row universe; ≥9 only 7 rows below gate. (2) Master source switched from 'Academy Award records' (superlatives-only article) to 'List of Academy Award–winning films' (cleaner Film/Year/Awards/Nominations table). (3) Everything Everywhere All at Once corrected from 8 Oscars (wrong) to 7 Oscars (audit-confirmed correct count); excluded from universe under the ≥8 threshold. (4) Director normalization uses semicolon-delimited source names for multi-director cells ('Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins' for West Side Story). (5) Best Picture column uses closed Yes/No vocabulary; Cabaret documented in normalization_decisions as the calibration row (only non-Best-Picture-winner in the ≥8 universe). Audit also confirmed: (i) aggregation category-fit is honest as pre-aggregated source-defined count (matches us_presidents_count_by_birth_state precedent); (ii) claim_type=source_defined is acceptable with explicit threshold filter; (iii) Cabaret is the strongest calibration case in the ≥8 universe.

Cycle-1 audit (2026-05-16): audit agent verdict 'Ready with residual hygiene' — 0 BLOCKING / 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE / 0 SUGGESTION. Both NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE findings addressed in cycle-1 prose-drift sweep across draft.json + curation.json: (1) stale 'wait' fragments + off-universe example references (Schindler's List, Best Years of Our Lives) and an incorrect Gravity '8-Oscars' phrasing (actual count is 7 Oscars) were removed/corrected throughout — draft.temporal_note Gravity '8-Oscars-non-Best-Picture' → '7-Oscars-non-Best-Picture'; draft._extraction_notes Schindler/Best-Years-of-Our-Lives 'wait' fragments replaced with Slumdog Millionaire/Gandhi examples; cur.decision_log Schindler 'wait' fragment replaced with Gone-with-the-Wind/Slumdog examples; cur.normalization_decisions Director paragraph dropped the Schindler 'wait' off-universe example and uses Danny Boyle (Slumdog Millionaire) instead; cur.open_questions Gravity '8-Oscars' → '7-Oscars'. (2) cur.source_coverage_notes 'Best Picture Winner status is cross-referenced from the master article's Best-Picture-winner column' framing was tightened to reflect the master article's actual layout — master uses Film/Year/Awards/Nominations columns plus Best-Picture styling cues to highlight Best Picture winners, with per-film article infobox 'Academy Awards'/'Best Picture' references serving as the per-row cross-verification. No CSV cell values, no schema/key/columns, no source_urls, no source_count, no per-row provenance pointers were changed in cycle-1; all 6 fixes are prose-only drift cleanup.
normalization_decisions:
Universe definition: the staged universe is the 15 films that have won at least 8 competitive Academy Awards per Wikipedia's 'List of Academy Award–winning films' master article. The universe rule is: 'film is in the master article's Film/Year/Awards/Nominations table AND total competitive Academy Award wins (Awards column) >= 8'. The threshold ≥8 was chosen after pre-staging audit comparison of 3 alternatives (≥7: 28 rows / ≥8: 15 rows / ≥9: 7 rows below gate) — ≥8 provides the cleanest 'most-awarded films' interpretation with one strong calibration case (Cabaret 1972). Awards count is COMPETITIVE Academy Award wins only — honorary Oscars, special achievement awards, and Best Foreign Language Film submissions are NOT counted per Wikipedia master article convention.

Film name normalization: each row's Film is taken verbatim from the per-film Wikipedia article's canonical title. Long titles preserved: 'The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King' (full series-and-subtitle form); 'Gone with the Wind' (the film, not the novel); 'The Last Emperor' (1987 Bernardo Bertolucci film); 'The English Patient' (1996 film). Disambiguation-suffix-free where possible: 'Ben-Hur' (1959 film) staged as bare 'Ben-Hur'; 'Titanic' (1997 film) staged as bare 'Titanic' despite multiple Titanic films existing per Wikipedia disambiguation page (the canonical 11-Oscar 1997 film is unambiguous in benchmark context).

Year of Release normalization: each row's Year is the integer year of theatrical release per the per-film Wikipedia article infobox. For films with multiple national release dates (e.g., West Side Story 1961 US premiere vs international releases), the US theatrical-release year is used per the master article convention.

Total Oscars Won normalization: each row's Total Oscars Won is the integer COUNT of competitive Academy Award wins per the master article's Awards column. This is a PRE-AGGREGATED COUNT — the master article supplies the count value rather than requiring the model to count from raw per-award rows. Mirror precedent: us_presidents_count_by_birth_state's Count cell. Distribution: 3 films with 11 (Ben-Hur, Titanic, LOTR Return), 1 film with 10 (West Side Story), 3 films with 9 (Gigi, The Last Emperor, The English Patient), 8 films with 8 (Gone with the Wind, From Here to Eternity, On the Waterfront, My Fair Lady, Cabaret, Gandhi, Amadeus, Slumdog Millionaire).

Best Picture Winner normalization: closed 2-value Yes/No vocabulary. Cabaret (1972) is the ONLY 'No' value in the universe — it won 8 competitive Oscars (including Best Director for Bob Fosse and Best Actress for Liza Minnelli) but lost Best Picture to The Godfather (1972). All other 14 films in the universe won Best Picture in addition to their other competitive Oscars. The Cabaret calibration case tests whether LLMs correctly distinguish multi-Oscar-but-non-Best-Picture from the more-common multi-Oscar-and-Best-Picture pattern.

Director normalization: each row's Director is taken from the per-film Wikipedia article infobox 'Directed by' field. Single-director films use the bare director name (e.g., 'William Wyler' for Ben-Hur; 'James Cameron' for Titanic; 'Peter Jackson' for LOTR Return; 'Bob Fosse' for Cabaret; 'Danny Boyle' for Slumdog Millionaire). Multi-director films use semicolon-delimited names per audit-recommended format: West Side Story (1961) has 'Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins' per the per-film article's co-director credit (Wise directed the non-dance scenes while Robbins directed the dance/musical numbers; both shared the Best Director Oscar). Diacritic preservation: 'Miloš Forman' for Amadeus (1984) per per-film article canonical form.

Sort order: CSV is sorted by Total Oscars Won descending (primary), then Year of Release ascending (within-tie secondary). Sort produces: Ben-Hur 1959 (11 Oscars) → Titanic 1997 (11) → LOTR Return 2003 (11) → West Side Story 1961 (10) → Gigi 1958 (9) → Last Emperor 1987 (9) → English Patient 1996 (9) → Gone with the Wind 1939 (8) → From Here to Eternity 1953 (8) → On the Waterfront 1954 (8) → My Fair Lady 1964 (8) → Cabaret 1972 (8) → Gandhi 1982 (8) → Amadeus 1984 (8) → Slumdog Millionaire 2008 (8). This deterministic sort matches the natural 'most-awarded films first' narrative dimension of the aggregation-category instance.
open_questions: 1. Whether the threshold should be ≥8 (current, 15 rows) or ≥7 (28 rows including Oppenheimer 2023 + Gravity 2013 7-Oscars-non-Best-Picture) or a different cutoff. Audit recommended ≥8 for the cleanest universe + strongest calibration case (Cabaret). 2. Whether Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022, 7 Oscars) should be added if the threshold lowers to ≥7. The proposed ≥8 design excludes EEAAO. 3. Whether the Best Picture Winner column should use Yes/No (current, closed vocab) or 'Won' / 'Not won' or boolean True/False — current Yes/No is audit-approved. 4. Whether West Side Story's Director should be 'Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins' (current, semicolon-delim per audit recommendation) or 'Robert Wise' (primary director only) or 'Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins'. 5. Whether the Total Oscars Won cell should be the COMPETITIVE-only count (current, per master article convention) or include honorary Oscars / special achievement awards (would inflate counts but is non-standard). 6. Whether the Cabaret calibration row should be flagged with a special-case marker (e.g., a separate 'Calibration Case' column) or kept as a regular row with the calibration role documented only in normalization_decisions (current staging). 7. Whether the sort should be Total Oscars descending (current, natural ranking) or alphabetical by Film name (benchmark default for qualitative). The aggregation-category natural-ranking convention is followed. 8. Whether the Year of Release should be theatrical-release year or Academy Awards ceremony year (the year of the awards) — current uses theatrical-release per per-film infobox convention; mirror precedents (Booker / Pulitzer) use ceremony year, but for films-by-Oscars-won the release-year is more natural since the ceremony year is usually 1 year later.
